reviews.review: This game has more content than some contemporary AAA titles, let alone other Early Access games. Absolute no-brainer.

At first glance, I didn't think I was going to like this game. 
My fiance and I were looking for something new to play together and he actually suggested this to me.
Its crazy fun and addicting. Its one of my go-tos for passing time or a quick change of pace. 
There's tons of missions and zones to explore, gather different minerals to craft and upgrade your weapons over 4 different classes. Fight swarms of deadly bugs in dangerous depths! 

Definitely worth a buy. 

The developers are doing an amazing job with this game by the way!

Rock and stone! :goldvein:

[spoiler] Buy it! [/spoiler]

TL;DR: What do you get when you crossbreed "Red Faction" with "Aliens" and throw some dwarves with guns into the mix? I haven't a clue... but it sounds fück!ng awesome!

[h1]What's this all about?[/h1]

You're a dwarf. A space dwarf, working on an orbital mining station, whose sole task is to get sent to the caverns on the planet below, explore them and mine the quota of rare minerals. Some deposits are hard to reach and present a logistical problem, which can be solved by generous application of grappling hooks or ziplines or by brute force mining. It would be a simple and rewarding job... if not for the local fauna, with teeth and claws straight outta hell, which will interrupt any and all mining attempts.
The game comprises randomly generated missions, mainly consisting of a procedurally generated cave, where you have to find, mine and store in a handy four-legged dumpster (think Terry Pratchett's Luggage but with less intelligence and utility) some minerals. Sometimes you'll mount a rescue mission only to find out that everyone is missing and all equipment is damaged. Sometimes you're sent as pest control team, where the pest in question is an order of magnitude larger than what you've encountered so far. But mostly it's about mining. The quotas are generous and the caves are dark and deep...
The missions start and finish on the janky, dilapidated Space Rig, which has everything a dwarf needs to thrive and survive - a bunk to sleep, a bar to get sloshed, barrels to kick about and a drop pod to get to the action. You can choose between four distinctive classes, which are designed to complement each other in a 2-4 player coop. Each class has unique weapons and abilities and enough perks and unlocks to choose from to keep the gameplay relevant. If you're an sp gamer at heart you will probably welcome the fact that every mission can be played [b]solo[/b] and you'll get a companion drone to help with the mining and fighting.
The world is fully destructible. I know plenty of games now include this feature, but it's just so fitting in this setting. The egg is stuck behind a rocky pillar? No problem bucko!

[h1]This game sounds meaningless. Is it grindy?[/h1]

I think the correct term here is "mine-y" not "grind-y". How else would you expect to get the minerals from the nodes, hmm?
And yes, I can envisage it being a bit repetitive and grindy after a while. The content isn't infinite you know and there isn't really a story there. But DRG strikes a perfect balance between living on borrowed time down in the caves and advancing your dwarf of choice through plethora of perks, equipment and unlockable cosmetics. 
In a way, DRG's main gameplay loop reminds me of the ancient Heavy Gear game and its Career Mode, where all you'd do is go on interconnected string of missions and advance through the ranks. Seemingly pointless, but rewarding in itself.

[h1]It is Early Access. Does it have bugs?[/h1]

Oh, yessss, it haz bugs! Dozens. [b]Hundreds[/b] even! More than you can shake your boomstick at!
They come in different forms, from small maggots, to leaping youngsters (which are enormously satisfying to take down mid-flight with a well aimed shot) all the way through to lumbering, heavily armed behemoths which make barrels of your trusty minigun glow red with rage.
Apart from this there are some weird graphical artefact leftovers here and there, mainly after you've just mined something, and some stuttering when using ground-piercing scanners, but nothing major.

[h1]But it's Early Access! Unfinished and buggy![/h1]

Nah. It's at the end of its roadmap anyway and what's there already is worth [b]every penny[/b] you spend on it and more.
Remember the hype built around many AAA+ titles these days? How big companies pour annual budget of some "third world" countries worth of dollars into marketing... and all that comes out is an unpolished turd propped with 12GB "day one patch" and pay-to-unlock content?
Well, this here game is nothing of the sort. It is, in my most humble opinion, an absolute gem and its reputation is well earned. Spread the word.

You and your friends are dropped via a drop pod onto some god forsaken planet into some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cave. Your job: secure whatever materials you find, and do whatever management tells you and try not to fall off cliffs. Also did I mention bugs? There's a lot of bugs...and we hate bugs. Luckily management has given you the right tools for the job...maybe. Sounds easy and simple right? Anyways rock and stone dwarven brothers.
